minutes.headline: Commissioners drop plans to seek PFAS-treatment funding this cycle, will survey residents on cost vs. hardness instead
minutes.summary: Tighe & Bond presented cost and feasibility scenarios for treating PFAS (and hardness) at the Keating and Lancaster A/B wells, and walked through the tightening EPA/MassDEP compliance timeline. After extensive public questioning, the commissioners concluded there was too little time and too many unknowns to apply for SRF funding this year, and decided instead to send residents a survey on priorities (cost, hardness, PFAS) before committing to a treatment path. The board also approved a radio system upgrade tied to the town's project, reviewed the Woodlands condo kayak-rack easement dispute, and heard the superintendent's report on a water main break during a mutual-aid fire response and the district's first PFAS litigation settlement payment.

public_comment.topic: Questioned the PFAS data behind the well scenarios, the four-parts-per-trillion running-average standard, and proposed an unlisted 'scenario six' piping Lancaster water to Keating.
Urged the district to include a cost-tradeoff question in the survey -- lower water bill vs. treating hardness vs. PFAS -- so residents understand what they are actually choosing between.

public_comment.topic: Asked whether Lunenburg qualifies as a 'rural community' for a possible grant to help pay for the radio system upgrade.

votes.motion: Reappoint district employees: superintendent Fran G. Mcame, clerk treasurer Christina Schwinger, office assistant Lisa M. [surname unclear], water utility operators Terry Truax, Philip Martinez and Ryan Goodman, and counsel.
Accept the proposal from Modular Communications for the radio system upgrade, using maintenance/equipment budget for the amount above the funded article, and pursue possible grant funding.

budget_items.topic: SRF funding application timeline for well treatment
budget_items.what_was_said: Tighe & Bond said SRF applications typically open in June and were due in July the prior year, so the board would need to decide soon whether to reapply for state funding.

budget_items.topic: Scenario four (treat Keating well for PFAS only) cost
budget_items.what_was_said: A commissioner and the engineers confirmed the capital cost estimate to treat only the Keating well for PFAS under scenario four.

budget_items.topic: Piping Lancaster wells to Keating (proposed scenario six)
budget_items.what_was_said: A commissioner estimated roughly this additional cost to pipe Lancaster A water to the Keating site to combine with a treatment plant there.

Engineers said the current bipartisan infrastructure law funding for PFAS remediation runs through 2026, so this year's application is likely the last round of guaranteed federal funding unless Congress reauthorizes it.

The project was originally estimated and funded by town meeting article at lower figures, but came in somewhat higher after adding a radio at town hall to fix a dead spot, tied to the town and fire/police system upgrade.

The commissioner moved to accept the vendor proposal, stating the dollar figure twice with slightly different renderings, with any shortfall to come from the maintenance/equipment budget line and possible grant reimbursement.

budget_items.topic: Hydrant fee vs. main break repair cost
budget_items.what_was_said: The superintendent said the recent main break repair cost roughly the first figure while the district's total annual hydrant fee charged to the town is only the second figure, arguing the fee needs to be raised substantially.

The district received its first PFAS litigation payment from 3M, described as the first of ten payments over ten years, with a separate DuPont settlement still to be paid out; a new general ledger account was created to hold the funds.
A commissioner estimated a heavy-duty trailer to store the trench box and main-break equipment could be purchased for around this figure, already anticipated in this year's budget.

transfers.description: Cost of the radio system proposal above the $40,000 town-meeting article, to be covered from the upgrade of equipment and services / maintenance budget line

decisions.decision: The board decided not to apply for SRF funding this year for well/PFAS treatment, citing insufficient time and too many unresolved unknowns.
The board directed the consultant (Nicole/Capital Strategic) to prepare a public survey on treatment scenarios, hardness, cost and PFAS concerns rather than hold a single special meeting.

The board agreed to send a letter to the Woodlands condo trustees' attorney requesting the kayak rack be resolved/removed from the district easement by July 1st, rather than the September date requested.
The board agreed to look into purchasing a larger trailer to store trench-box and main-break equipment for faster response.
The district will check whether Lunenburg qualifies for a rural-community grant to help offset the radio system upgrade cost, while proceeding with the purchase regardless.

what_happened.line: Commissioners decided not to apply this year for state SRF funding to treat PFAS and hardness at the Keating and Lancaster wells, citing insufficient time and unresolved unknowns.
Instead of a treatment decision, the board directed its consultant to prepare a resident survey on cost, hardness and PFAS priorities before choosing a path.
The board approved a radio system upgrade proposal from Modular Communications, tied to the town's broader communications project, with a possible grant offset.
The board agreed to send a letter asking Woodlands condo trustees to remove a kayak rack from the district's easement by July 1st.
The district reported receiving the first of ten annual PFAS litigation settlement payments from 3M, with a separate DuPont settlement still pending.

why_it_matters: Passing on this year's SRF application delays any well-treatment decision by at least a cycle, and engineers said current federal infrastructure-law funding for PFAS remediation is not guaranteed past 2026, so the timing affects what a future warrant article could ask residents to pay.
The coming survey is how residents will be asked to weigh a lower water bill against treating hardness and against treating PFAS, so its questions will shape any future treatment proposal.
The superintendent flagged that the hydrant fee the district charges the town may need to rise substantially, which would touch the town's own budget rather than water ratepayers alone.
